summary:
plan.md is written (no build or render yet). The obelisk stands 7x7 at x47..53, z47..53 on the y5 summit, steps in to 5x5 at y38 and ends in a pyramid of stairs with a dark tip at y76. Lower 19 courses smooth_quartz, the rest calcite/smooth_sandstone courses: a sharp colour line at y25.
It reads as the Washington Monument by silhouette: a plain white needle on a round granite plaza, ringed by 50 end-rod flagpoles at r16 with stars-and-stripes banners, a great ring walk around the knoll and Mall walks running east-west. Warm froglights sit at its base for dusk. Smooth 7→5 wide marble obelisk (pale quartz to y24, cream calcite/sandstone above, stair pyramidion to y76) on a mapped grassy knoll. Round granite plaza with seating arcs and a pavilion, 50-pole flag ring, radiating walks, lamps, froglight floodlights, edge trees and a corner lodge.
Six parts: ground, obelisk, plaza, flags, walks and trees, lodge. No interior rooms.
elements: walks, lamps, lawn lights and trees (parts/walks-trees.mjs)

summary: ground and knoll: parts/ground.mjs lays all 10,000 columns from the height map with groundColumn (stone, dirt, grass_block). make.sh gives a whole build.nbt of about 41k blocks. I did not render the ground or run `mcd check`/`mcd fit`.

obelisk: Obelisk built in parts/obelisk.mjs: 7x7 quartz shaft y6..24, cream courses y25..37, taper wash y38, 5x5 shaft y39..68, windows y66 and red/glowstone lights y67, stepped pyramidion y69..76 with chain tip. make.sh gives 2415 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette; check and fit are clean.
polish: The render shows the obelisk on the stub ground, not the real knoll; that is for the merge.
Plan says one stepped taper at y38; the brief's wording says every even course. I followed plan.md; a reviewer should confirm.
chain is not in the toolkit's version list (it knows iron_chain); placed as chain per plan.md, check at delivery for 1.21.1.

waste.what: Worked out the 7x7/5x5 course coordinates and the window and light cells by hand before calling the helpers.
waste.cost: about 5 minutes of reasoning, no retries
waste.tool: A plan-to-build table: a helper that reads the obelisk constants from plan.md and emits the course list.

waste.what: vocab.mjs export * silently makes h1 and h2 clashing names unimportable from the barrel; had to import from vocab/h1.mjs directly.
waste.cost: one failed guess at the barrel import, then a read of both files
waste.tool: Distinct names or one module per helper family in vocab.mjs.

companions.task: Check the taper wash and pyramidion slope so each stair course reads as one clean face and the y24/25 seam is crisp.
Light the obelisk base for the dusk floodlight plan, with no mob spawn on the plaza side.

summary:
plaza and pavilion: Plaza and pavilion built in parts/plaza.mjs: round smooth-stone plaza at y5 with polished andesite bands and obelisk surround, 8 seating-wall arcs at y6 with lanterns, screening pavilion at x54..58 z49..52 (floor y5, walls y6..7, roof y8).
make.sh saves a whole build.nbt; plaza line reports 423 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette. check finds no floating blocks; fit is OK; zoom renders read as a plaza, arcs and pavilion.
Left the 11 RESERVED floodlight cells at y5 unwritten for the flag part; plan.md Notes and elements.md rows 10-12 are updated.
polish: The 11 RESERVED floodlight cells at y5 (49..51,5,45), (49..51,5,55), (45,5,49..51), (54,5,47), (54,5,53) are left as grass by this part; the flag part must place its ochre_froglight there with over: true, or they stay grass inside the plaza.
Seating ring and pavilion were rendered and read well; the pavilion roof field is a bottom slab over the interior air, as the plan specifies, and fit does not flag it.

waste.what: Worked out the plaza disc, banding rings and obelisk-surround cell sets by hand, with a local disc() loop, because plazaDisc has no skip predicate for the reserved floodlight cells
waste.cost: one module rewrite and one fix (the pavilion floor was wrongly excluded from the first disc)
waste.tool: plazaDisc (h1) with a keep/skip option, or a reserved-cell mask passed to the build library so parts can leave cells unwritten

waste.what: Imported from vocab/h1.mjs and vocab/base.mjs by hand because vocab.mjs star-exports h1 and h2, which define the same helper names (plazaDisc, pavilionBox, floodlight, lampPost, shaftCourse, obsWindows, lodgeHip), so the names are ambiguous
waste.cost: one failed assumption read from the kit, about 2 minutes
waste.tool: a single vocab.mjs that exports one version of each helper, or distinct names per module

waste.what: Checked the zoom renders and fit output by eye, with no check that the pavilion roof field and seating slabs sit on what they should
waste.cost: three renders and a fit run
waste.tool: a plan-vs-build assertion script that reads plan.md coordinates for the element and reports mismatches

companions.task: Lay the seating-wall arcs and the plaza banding and check the arc gap widths and end blocks against the plan's ring geometry.
Fit the pavilion's glass bands on the north and south faces and check the 2-high east door opening.

summary:
flag ring and floodlights: parts/flags.mjs builds the flag ring: a white_concrete_powder walk on 15.5<=r<17.5 at y5 (585 blocks placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette).
Fifty flagPoles at r=16 (end_rod y6..10, white_concrete cap y11, red/blue white_wall_banner outward) with an ochre_froglight flush under each foot, plus the 11 reserved base floodlights.
make.sh leaves a whole build.nbt; check shows no floating or unsupported blocks, fit is OK, and the zoomed renders read as a white ring of poles with banners.
polish: Base floodlights (FLOODLIGHTS, 11 cells) sit inside the plaza disc: runParts will refuse them if the plaza part paves those cells first. The plaza part must leave (49..51,5,45), (49..51,5,55), (45,5,49..51), (54,5,47), (54,5,53) as air or let them through; the plan's Notes now say so. Not verified here: the plaza part is a stub in this copy.
Element 21 (no-spawn lighting) is only partly met: the flag ring is lit (50 foot froglights, ~2-block spacing), but the whole-site check belongs to the walks and lamps part.
The flag ring is not checked against the walks part, which is still a stub here. The Mall walk will stop at the ring walk at x 33..34 and 66..67 (z 49..51); the pole cells at y6..11 must stay free.

waste.what: Worked out the 50 pole foot cells by hand, duplicating flagPole's angle and rounding so each froglight lands under its pole.
waste.cost: one extra loop in flags.mjs plus a rounding re-check; a mismatch would put lights in the wrong cells
waste.tool: a flagPole helper that returns its foot cell (or a poleCells(count, cx, cz, r) helper) so callers do not recompute the rounding

waste.what: Ring heights and radius bands were checked with a throwaway node one-liner, and the walk/banner collisions with the Mall walk were found by hand.
waste.cost: one ad-hoc script and about four minutes of coordinate reasoning
waste.tool: mcd plan (or a band report) that prints the surface height and part ownership for an r-band, and lists cells two parts both want

waste.what: vocab.mjs star-exports floodlight from both h1 and h2, which breaks ESM import of the whole vocab module. I had to import from vocab/h1.mjs by name, after a failed make run.
waste.cost: one failed make.sh run and a re-run
waste.tool: vocab.mjs should export each name once (drop the duplicate from h2 or rename it), so that `import { floodlight } from "../vocab.mjs"` works

waste.what: Confirmed the flag ring by eye from two zoomed renders, with no top-down view of the ring, so the radius band and pole spacing were judged from oblique shots.
waste.cost: two zoom renders and a few reads of PNG tiles
waste.tool: a top-down plan render (`mcd render --top` or a plan-view tile) so ring spacing can be checked at a glance

summary: walks, lamps, lawn lights and trees: Walks, lamps, lawn lights and 12 edge oaks are built in parts/walks-trees.mjs: 1215 walk cells (Mall E/W, N/S, four diagonals, great ring) with 193 slab half steps, 45 lamp posts, 48 lawn froglights, 12 oaks. make.sh saves a whole build.nbt with no refused writes and no off-palette blocks; check reports no floating blocks and the walks walkable end to end.
polish: The great ring (r 31..33) reads as a dark dotted band in the iso render rather than a clean white ring; I did not zoom in to confirm whether that is the slab/step pattern or the lamps, so it needs a close-up tile.
Lamps on the great ring (radius 30 and 34) and the diagonal lamps are placed by formula and not checked by eye.
Tree crowns leave 40 'orphan' oak_leaves that touch only the trunk; they are normal for oaks, but the check still lists them.
vocab.mjs leaves floodlight and lampPost ambiguous (h1 and h2 both export them); this part imports from vocab/h1.mjs directly. Noted in plan.md Notes, not fixed in the shared vocab.

waste.what: Walk networks written by hand: 2-wide diagonal bands (sign/offset arithmetic per corner), the great ring by radius test, and lamp offsets for each walk side and diagonal.
waste.cost: about 120 lines of coordinate code, two rewrites of the diagonal lamp formula
waste.tool: A build-library helper such as walkLine(g, from, to, width, {every: 9, lamp: 'alternate'}) and walkArc(g, centre, r0, r1, every), so a walk is one call with its endpoints and width.

waste.what: Probing the surface and checking what an earlier part laid by hand with a throwaway script (block at h, block at h+1, ring cell heights).
waste.tool: mcd cell build.nbt x,y,z (block, state and neighbours) or a surface-of-column query, to answer 'what is at this cell' without a script.

waste.what: Found by trial that vocab.mjs's export * leaves floodlight and lampPost ambiguous, so named imports return undefined; had to import from vocab/h1.mjs.
waste.cost: one failed import test, then a direct-path import
waste.tool: Rename or dedupe the h2 helpers in vocab.mjs (or add a test that fails on duplicate export names) so the clash is caught before parts start.

waste.what: Checked the look by eye in a 5-tile sheet only; no close-up of the ring or lamp rows.
waste.cost: one render, one read of the sheet
waste.tool: mcd render --closeups with a tile at the great ring and one at a lamp row, so a part's own detail is checked without extra steps.

companions.task: Lay out the diagonal and great-ring walk lines and the lamp offsets from the site survey, so the 2-wide bands and the radii come from a survey, not from arithmetic in the generator.
Choose the 12 edge oak positions and check the crowns clear the walks and lawn lights and leave room to grow.

summary:
survey lodge: Survey Lodge built in parts/lodge.mjs: stone_bricks walls y3..4 on the 3x2 in-plot footprint (x83..85, z98..99), glass_pane slit at (83,4,99), and a stone_brick_stairs roof at y5 faced inward so it rises to a ridge. ./make.sh gives a whole build.nbt with 18 lodge blocks, no refused writes and no off-palette blocks; check shows nothing floating or unsupported.
Plan.md checklist and elements.md item 20 ticked; the Notes record the lodgeHip name collision and the roof-facing departure from the plan.
polish: Light check not closed: the lodge adds no light source, and the probe at y3 showed 0 sources only because the other parts are still stubs. Re-run `mcd light build.nbt --y 3` after parts 4-5 land and check the lodge's floor cells.
Roof departs from the plan's `facing outward`: the stairs face inward, because outward sags the 2-deep footprint into a trough (recorded in plan.md Notes). Lead to confirm.
No ridge slab: the 3x2 footprint has no interior cells, so the h2 helper places only perimeter stairs and walls.
No quoins, sill or string course; the corner stairs are straight, not hip corners. Polish, not blocking.
vocab.mjs has an ambiguous lodgeHip export (h1 and h2 both define it); I imported from vocab/h2.mjs directly. The shared vocab needs a fix.

waste.what: lodgeHip is exported by both vocab/h1.mjs and vocab/h2.mjs, and vocab.mjs does `export *` from both, so the name is silently ambiguous and undefined through vocab.mjs. I had to find this by testing typeof and import the h2 version directly.
waste.tool: Rename one helper (e.g. lodgeHipH1) or drop the stale h1 export; a `make.sh` or vocab check that fails on duplicate exported names would catch it.

waste.what: The lodgeHip roof faces its stairs outward, which sags a 2-deep footprint into a trough. I only saw it in a side render, then re-laid all 6 roof cells by hand with g.set.
waste.cost: 2 renders, 6 stairs re-set by hand, one rebuild
waste.tool: A lodgeHip option for roof facing (inward, or a ridge for footprints 2 deep), or a `mcd fit` rule that flags a roof whose middle is lower than its eaves.

waste.what: Checking the lodge's roof profile and light by eye: zoom renders from two sides, plus a light probe that shows 0 sources only because the other parts are still stubs.
waste.cost: 3 renders and a light probe, judged by eye
waste.tool: `mcd zoom --from` already exists; a profile check for stairs or roof shape in `mcd check` would make the roof read deterministic.

companions.task: The corner shapes of the stone-brick hip (outer_left and outer_right stairs at the four corners) and the ridge seam where the north and south rows meet, so the hip turns at the corners instead of ending square.
The lodge's own light: a lantern or lit slit, since the lodge adds no light source. Then confirm the dark-cell count at the lodge's floor once the lamps and lawn lights from parts 4-5 are in.
Quoins at the corners, a sill under the slit and a string course at the wall top, to make the 2-storey stone box read as built rather than a plain block.

summary: inspection: walk ok and fit OK, nothing to fix
